# September playlist: source evidence, Jet gaps, and owner choices

Dated evidence: 2026-09-09. Scope: the 14-video [Jet research playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLXgiJybdlzvk). This is a mining report, not an implementation release or performance victory claim.

## Verdict

The common failure is **multiple places that must agree about one fact, without a reliable check that they still agree**. It appears as duplicated ordering rules, competing UI state, ambiguous performance measurements, false coverage confidence, hidden initialization, and progress displays that replace observations with expectations. Shorter code, more tests, native compilation, and more abstraction do not independently solve it.

Jet has useful foundations: checked types and effects, one semantic model across execution modes, source-linked tools, structured tests, typed host output, and one UI tree. Several foundations are already implemented. That is not end-to-end proof: the fresh compiler build failed; an explicitly identified older binary rejected several shipped examples; current host progress source loses observed count information. Missing public progress and native host contracts are separate from those defects.

This run created **19 coherent follow-up cards, #2990–#3008, and 10 unratified ballots**. Existing mechanisms retain their existing owners. No compiler, runtime, or language implementation change was authorized or made by this audit. Closing the research does not close its recommendations.

## Evidence boundaries

- The full captured transcript argument of every video was reviewed, alongside stratified audience samples and linked technical sources. Thirteen caption tracks are automatic; one is creator-provided. Automatic captions and OCR alone do not establish high-confidence technical facts.
- Retrieval and review are different counts. Comments were sampled from high-reaction roots, recent roots, low-visibility technical items, substantive replies, and disagreements. Neither the sample nor keyword counts are a poll. Audience identities are omitted; an uploader reply is identified by role only when credibility depends on that role.
- Visual review was selective, not frame-by-frame. There are 169 retained OCR review records plus 20 manually read selected frames, from 189 captured frames. On-screen spellings were checked where captured; an unshown interaction is not evidence of its outcome. Caption row timestamps are start times, not a percentage of the video reviewed.
- YouTube browser startup failed in this environment. Metadata, captions, comments, and media were captured through the available read and yt-dlp paths. Retrieval warnings and unresolved primary references are retained below. No authenticated playlist mutation occurred.
- Linked current documentation can differ from a video's recorded version. Wails prerelease state, TypeScript preview claims, and Solid/HTMX version facts are dated separately from demonstrations. A README, release note, or video title is not a benchmark receipt.
- The last successful Jet binary used for the explicit contrast probes has SHA-256 `ef7c0fcc8a697038a42558272a015fbb104915fa4bc347234f78a94207de182a`. The attempted rebuild failed. Every result from that binary is prior-build evidence, not proof of the present checkout. Fresh standalone C++ and Rust-host probes are identified separately.

## Verified defects and counterexamples

| Finding | Observed contrast | Meaning and owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F01 — Fresh compiler build | Six E0425 errors reference missing `jet_std::decode_int_with` from `Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingTraits.rs`, included by the Web host. | Current-source build blocker, not a hypothetical runtime issue. #2990 under #2919. |
| F02 — Complexity fixture | The checked-in negative fixture reached E0080 for retired record-body spelling before the intended lint. An isolated current-body probe reached L2902, score 4; the refactored fixture scored lower. | Repair the fixture and assert the intended diagnostic, not merely a nonzero exit. #2991. This is not a claim that the suite falsely passed. |
| F03 — Duplicated policy | `optimistic_rank` and `persisted_rank` both scored 0. Their consumer printed `false` in default run and interpreter. | Complexity is not an agreement oracle. Architecture advice must show a counterexample and the duplicated rule, not a magic score. #2998; prior-build evidence. |
| F04 — Constructor facts | Clock seam and task-group probes failed before the intended behavior; the task group ICE reported a `Duration` constructor without a resolved return type. | Fix checked return facts before interpreting runtime behavior. #2992. Default run and interpreter both exited 101 on the task-group probe; prior-build evidence. |
| F05 — Pool identity | `pool_stale_id.jet` ICEd on a write-call argument with no checked place. | The intended stale-ID behavior was never reached. #2993; prior-build evidence. |
| F06 — Directory walk | `grep_scan.jet` produced E0302 on `entry.is_dir` and E1220 for `Time.Wait`. | Reconcile actual directory-entry and authority contracts; do not suppress checks to green the example. #2994; prior-build evidence. |
| F07 — Iterator progress | `progress.jet` produced E2402 for `ParseError` to `Err`, plus E1220 for `Time.Wait`. | Resolve example/API/effect agreement; this does not prove the progress implementation itself is absent. #2995; prior-build evidence. |
| F08 — Generic module value | `generic_modules.jet` rejected `Mode.Fast` with E0857, followed by unresolved `values`. | Resolve enum value facts at the existing compile-time module boundary. #2996; prior-build evidence. |
| F09 — Progress count truth | Fresh actual Rust host source: adding 11 to total 10 reports completed 10; finishing at 3 reports completed 10; lowering total to 1 reports completed 1. | The model substitutes/clamps counts, separately from terminal rendering. #3008 and D-PROGRESS-COUNTS1 ask whether to preserve observation, reject inconsistent updates, or retain current completion semantics. No choice is ratified here. |
| F10 — Branch coverage is not independence | For `a and (b or c)`, a two-case set reaches both decision outcomes but does not establish every condition's independent effect. A four-case witness set does. | A logical counterexample, not a Jet MC/DC runtime claim. Jet already has branch/outcome rows (#1904). Optional condition-independence evidence is the separate #3002 choice. |
| F11 — C++ initialization | Fresh C++20/O2/threaded probe printed `attempts=2 total=336 constant=42`; disassembly showed a guarded dynamic initializer and a constant-return fast path. | Dynamic initialization synchronizes and retries after an exception; constant initialization does not imply the same guard. Do not report that every static variable locks on every access. |

The duplicate-rule consumer is deliberately small:

```jet
fn optimistic_rank(after: Int) Int -> after + 1
fn persisted_rank(after: Int) Int -> after + 2
fn run() -> print(optimistic_rank(10) == persisted_rank(10))
```

Observed commands: `jet lint --complexity <file> --json` reported score 0 for both helpers; `jet run <file>` and `jet run <file> --interpret` printed `false`. These are evidence of the lint's boundary, not proof that Jet should infer arbitrary business intent.

## De-slop: direct answers for Jet and every Jet codebase

The video's substantive example is not “ask an agent to refactor.” An ordering rule appeared in multiple files and on both sides of optimistic/persisted behavior. A deeper insertion-point module could own the invariant. The exact seam depends on the consumer: a resolver that repeatedly branches on caller mode can merely move the duplication. The proposed module's name and file count do not prove it is deep.

| Level | Jet implementation | All software written in Jet | Product nudge and proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Strategic | Give each semantic fact one authority: syntax registry, sema facts, shared Prelude policy, query graph. A second implementation is not a shortcut. | Name the business outcome and invariants before selecting folders or classes. “Optimistic and persisted order agree” is an outcome; “has a service layer” is not. | Existing effects, authority and semantic inspection provide facts. Proposed architecture advice (#2998) must be advisory or explicit policy, never a claim to know the owner's intent. |
| Operational | Put a seam around a coherent rule and its dependencies. Separate front-end facts from host lowering without re-encoding policy. | Choose the boundary from changes and consumer behavior: insertion, payment, booking, reconciliation. Keep one rule usable by multiple adapters. | Show the paths that must agree, the reason they agree, and an executable disagreement. D-ARCH-ADVICE1 compares advisory evidence, explicit project policy, and no new product advice. |
| Tactical | Test the consumer outcome, not source text, field copies, forwarding, or any-failure-is-success. The broken complexity fixture and constructor facts are concrete repairs. | Inject clock/IO boundaries where deterministic tests need them; retain one intent-bearing counterexample across a refactor. Do not introduce an interface for a single speculative caller. | Existing test effects (#1916), complexity lint (#2033), and inspector remain the mechanisms. #2991–#2993 repair demonstrated blockers; no second mocking or architecture engine. |

**Features that encourage the positive:** evidence-backed inspection of repeated rules and agreement boundaries; source-linked cost and workload facts; deterministic effect substitution; typed endpoint generation; precise failures tied to the consumer's invariant. Most mechanisms already exist. The architecture-advice surface is an owner choice, and reliable runtime evidence still matters.

**Features that make slop harder:** checked effects and authority budgets; one frontend and one semantic source across hosts; explicit typed failure handling; generated boundary contracts; stable source identities and invalidation; tests that fail on the wrong business result. They prevent classes of mistakes, not bad requirements. Neither a compiler nor an LLM can derive the intended rank formula from two arbitrary arithmetic functions.

**Beginner path:** write the direct program; receive a concrete diagnosis and one understandable repair. No mandatory policy file, architecture ceremony, or numeric quality score. **Expert path:** inspect exact edges, source locations, effects, cache identity, generated artifacts, and measured costs; opt into a project policy and reject a proposed seam with reasons. Both paths use the same facts.

The audience added useful cautions: source-text tests can preserve the wrong implementation; fewer lines or files can obscure a domain rule; shared vocabulary helps only when it refers to real behavior; a generated “deep module” can still have a shallow, mode-heavy interface. Likes do not validate any of these claims. The arithmetic contrast validates only the narrow statement that low complexity does not establish agreement.

## Wails V3: improvements, transfer, and a stronger Jet experience

Wails' useful improvements are an app graph separate from window creation, independently managed windows, services and generated bindings, typed app/window event facilities, frontend development feedback, platform packaging, and host services. Current primary sources corroborate the architecture. “Complete rewrite,” “faster,” small binary screenshots, and “Electron killer” are not matched performance evidence.

| Wails mechanism | Jet state at this audit | Transfer or better experience | Proof / disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `application.New`, `app.Window.NewWithOptions`, window lookup and close | Jet has an app graph and a native GTK renderer, but not a public multi-window lifetime contract. | One app-owned lifetime; scoped window handles; explicit close and app shutdown; shared UI state, not per-window competing loops. | #2999, D-UI-WINDOW-LIFE1. #3004 separately proves existing GTK behavior. |
| Services and generated client bindings | Typed handler-derived endpoint contracts already have owner #2962. | Derive boundary calls and errors from one checked definition. Do not add a second web mechanism because Wails generates TypeScript. | Existing #2962; fresh end-to-end proof belongs to the current proof campaign. |
| Window/app events and cleanup | Core UI has events and capabilities; GTK source currently owns one window. | App/window cleanup, callback cancellation, and resource lifetime must agree. A generic event bus is not a substitute for owned lifecycle. | #2999/#3004; existing platform service owner #2792. |
| Development frontend integration | Jet already owns HMR state preservation (#2465), pending boundaries (#2478), and a common devtools direction (#2423). | Preserve drafts, signals, focus and scroll; stale async results must not replace the latest result; report precise causes through the same tools. | Existing owners, not duplicate ballots. |
| `SystemTray`, `SetMenu`, `OnClick`, `Destroy` | The GUI battery's “tray fallback” is displayed text, not a tray API. | Typed actions and explicit unavailable capability; integrate lifetime with the app. Never silently substitute text for a tray service. | #3006, D-UI-TRAY1. |
| `WebviewWindow.Print()` | No matching public Jet native document-print contract was found. | Typed document request, actual user-controlled print UI, and truthful submitted/cancelled/unavailable outcome. Submission is not proof of physical printing. | #3007, D-UI-PRINT1. |
| Cross-platform build and prerelease guidance | GTK/Linux source is not macOS, Windows, or mobile proof. Native widgets are already ratified; a new renderer is not this choice. | One checked source and visible target capabilities; precise platform requirements and build artifacts. | Existing #2792/#2815; #3004. Performance cells remain #2858. |

**How Jet could beat Wails UX:** keep the UI tree, state, effects, data contracts, and diagnostics in one checked program; carry that program through native and web hosts; derive bindings and tool views rather than asking the developer to synchronize them. Beginners should get a working app without selecting several unrelated state systems. Experts should retain explicit platform, capability, lifecycle, generated-artifact, and performance control.

That is a proposed advantage, not a current win. Wails already offers lifecycle and host operations Jet lacks. The plain Jet GTK example must work, close cleanly, and preserve meaning across applicable modes before the stronger story is credible. A Go/Wails application can also improve its typed state and generated contracts; “two languages means inherently bad software” is not the finding.

## Version claims that remain uncorroborated

The web video discusses Solid 2 and HTMX 4. Captured upstream package/changelog material did not corroborate those releases; the tag API requests were forbidden. That is not proof that a tag or release does not exist. Treat the video’s specific new APIs as demonstrated/source-claimed surfaces, not verified currently shipped framework behavior. Wails beta status was separately corroborated by its current site and prerelease metadata. Retrieval counts matched the captured comment-count metadata, but complete reply-thread coverage was not independently established.

## Cross-resource synthesis and corrections

| Topic | Relationship | Resolved finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Boundaries and decomposition | De-slop, Big OOPs, and the compiler-port discussion recur; the two Casey talks are not independent speakers. | A boundary is valuable when it owns a rule. Hierarchy, class syntax, service names, and physical file splits are separate choices. |
| Measurement before optimization | Ripgrep, compiler speed, profiling history, static initialization, and tqdm overlap. | Measure the mechanism and workload; retain profile/target/backend/clock/coverage identity. Do not import headline ratios. |
| Evidence quality | SQLite, de-slop, compiler feedback, and local probes reinforce the need for discriminating checks. | Coverage, fault injection, fuzzing, differential tests, and counterexamples catch different failures. None is a universal quality percentage. |
| Runtime authority and state | Zig IO, native GUI services, web async state, and deterministic tests recur. | Make dependencies and ownership explicit without imposing an initialization framework on every small program. |
| Concision versus comprehensibility | Python compression and Rust learning create a real tension with abstraction enthusiasm. | Keep the beginner surface direct and diagnostic repair local. Shorter source is not necessarily easier to understand or safer to change. |
| Performance folklore | Profiling history and Big OOPs challenge familiar historical readings. | The original sources and dates control the historical claim. Commentary, quotation, OCR, and audience correction remain distinct evidence kinds. |

Important corrections:

1. A statically initialized C++ local is not the same mechanism as a dynamically initialized one. A guard fast path is not proof of a contended mutex on every access. The fresh contrast confirms both paths differ.
2. Knuth's familiar optimization sentence is not a blanket prohibition on performance reasoning. Workload frequency, measurement method, and the quoted historical context matter. Missing or inaccessible papers are not filled in from the speaker's confidence.
3. Encapsulation does not imply inheritance. A hierarchy can be a good domain model, a poor boundary, or unnecessary; those are separate questions. Do not replace dogmatic OOP with dogmatic anti-OOP.
4. Branch/outcome coverage already exists in Jet. Independent-condition evidence and bit-mask testing are not synonyms for it. A bitwise expression is one Boolean condition unless its bits are tested separately; short-circuit evidence must not evaluate skipped expressions.
5. Jet already has lazy iterator progress and a richer Rust host model. Missing Jet-callable manual lifecycle controls are a public API gap, not proof that all progress machinery is absent.
6. An OS shebang is launch metadata at byte zero, not a second Jet language. Kernel argument handling, `env -S`, PATH selection, installed interpreter version, and shell behavior are separate portability facts.
7. Wails beta/prerelease evidence is version-specific. Current docs can corroborate architecture without proving the video's performance or every host's behavior.
8. SQLite's reliability argument is about interacting methods and hostile failures, not worship of a test-count or coverage number. A reported high coverage percentage never licenses skipping crash/reopen behavior or semantic checks.

The exact-topic matrix in the retained appendix groups shared claims by stable upstream identity. Multiple talks repeating Knuth, the same Casey speaker, or the same docs do not become independent corroboration. Opposing stances are marked conflict and resolved with the claim-level corrections, not a vote.

The [resolved SQLite quicksort report](https://sqlite.org/bugs/info/2026-06-03T07:26:42Z) makes one further distinction important: its introsort/heap fallback preserves correctness; its separate coarse early-return cap knowingly permits partial sorting. The talk preferred recursing only on the smaller partition and looping over the larger one. Do not label every depth limit an incorrect fix.

## Ranked beat vectors — shipped mechanisms versus proposed advantage

| Rank | Vector and mechanism | Shipped or proposed | What a competitor would have to change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Language-owned facts and effects can keep one business rule checked across tooling and hosts. | Foundations implemented; complete behavior and new host contracts still require proof. | Go/Wails would need equivalent checked program-level authority beyond generated boundary types. A typed DSL can cover a subset; it does not check arbitrary application behavior. Rust already has strong type and safety machinery. |
| 2 | One semantic source across AOT, JIT, interpreter, and web avoids a separate policy implementation per host. | Ratified invariant I9 with existing implementation, not an audit-time all-mode pass. | A multi-runtime stack must share or translate the same policy and preserve observable meaning. This is architectural work, not a faster widget. |
| 3 | Source-linked failure, cost, and repair evidence can reduce the context an agent needs to make a safe change. | Existing inspector/trace/report seams; bounded source profiles and architecture advice are proposed. | Competitors can copy views; equivalent provenance and compiler facts must exist underneath. No categorical win is claimed from a UI alone. |
| 4 | Structured effect substitution plus crash/reopen and semantic differential checks can shorten reliable testing. | Fault effects and comparison machinery exist; storage-crash and SQL fuzz coverage is new work. | SQLite already has a stronger demonstrated testing tradition. Jet must match the hostile scenarios, not merely expose a prettier API. |
| 5 | One typed output and UI state model can reduce adapter disagreement. | Host output is real; public manual progress and native lifetime/tray/printing remain choices. | Wails, tqdm, and web frameworks already provide much of this surface. Most of this row is parity work that peers can also improve. |

Search speed, compile time, progress overhead, package size, and application responsiveness are **measurement gates**, not categorical victories. #2858 and #676 retain the paired-workload work. The strict comparator applies per cell and metric: Jet/non-Rust below 1.00; Jet/Rust no worse than 1.05 is noise-band parity, not a win. Wrong output, mismatched workloads, debug/release mixing, unavailable runs, and inconclusive evidence do not pass.

## Avoid list

| Mistake | Evidence | Jet exposure / disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Treat a low complexity score as correctness | The score-zero ordering disagreement | Exposed; #2998 advice must show a consumer counterexample. |
| Test source shape or accept any failure | De-slop audience concern and the E0080-before-L2902 fixture | Existing testing policy rejects it; actual fixture repair #2991. |
| Encode the same policy in several runtimes | UI/IO/compiler boundary examples | I9 rejects the architecture; host adapters still need exercised parity. #2919/#3004. |
| Make hierarchy the definition of a boundary | Big OOPs and linked historical material | Jet need not add inheritance machinery; keep modules, types, traits, and functions as their actual mechanisms. |
| Hide synchronization or misdescribe its cost | C++ guarded dynamic initialization versus constant path | Explain and measure actual initialization; never label every static a mutex operation. #2858. |
| Turn library adoption into mandatory framework setup | Zig IO and Wails initialization | Preserve useful direct defaults; expert selection through the existing seam. No speculative second IO system. |
| Let stale async work replace current state | Web pending/ordering surfaces | Existing pending/HMR owners #2478/#2465; prove transitions rather than count promises. |
| Import benchmark headlines | 8,000x search and 10x compiler titles | #2858/#676 require matched inputs, profiles, phases and outcomes. |
| Display expectations as observations | Fresh progress host contrast | Exposed at model level, not just renderer. #3008. |
| Advertise a platform fallback that is only text | Jet tray battery inspection | Exposed; #3006, distinct from actual dialogs/clipboard services. |
| Equate branch coverage with MC/DC or reliability | SQLite terminology and the Boolean witness contrast | Branch rows already exist; optional independent-condition evidence #3002; crash/fuzz #3000/#3001. |
| Compress source until evaluation order and state disappear | Python one-line examples and audience objections | Keep one canonical readable spelling and formatter; do not add golfing syntax or style variants. |
| Treat captions, OCR, or applause as truth | Historical quotations and sampled corrections | Evidence-process exposure, resolved by provenance, confidence limits, linked sources, and the retained claims. |
| Add public syntax to solve an instrumentation problem | Profiler and compiler-tooling proposals | Use the existing trace/query path first. No new keyword or recording trigger is proposed. |

## Agent-optimality: all five quantities

| Quantity | What the playlist changes | Jet assessment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verdict fidelity | SQLite's hostile tests and the score-zero disagreement distinguish a true consumer oracle from coverage or style proxies. | Weakest today: executable confidence. Build, constructor, and checked-place failures block meaningful verdicts. #2990–#2993, #3000–#3002. |
| Verdict latency | Native compiler ports, incremental feedback, profiling, and truthful progress can shorten or explain waiting. | Measure edit-to-verdict, not just backend throughput or CPU sums. No loop-speed win is claimed. #676/#2858. |
| Verdict actionability | Source-linked rules, typed errors and mapped editor ranges let the agent repair without guessing. | Current ICEs are honest internal failures, not actionable user errors. Bounded architecture evidence and embedded mappings are proposed. #2998/#3003. |
| Context economy | Rule-owning modules, concise diagnostics, generated contracts, and a small direct surface reduce tokens per correct change. | Fewer lines do not help if an agent must reconstruct order, state or hidden policy. Wails and Python show opposite ends of that risk. |
| Repair determinism | One mechanism and one authority reduce the number of plausible but incompatible repairs. | Preserve the shared frontend, effect, progress and UI models. Expert override stays explicit; proposed advice must expose evidence, not dictate intent. |

These are qualitative conclusions, not measured agent productivity ratios. A matched edit–run–repair study must hold workload, starting state, tool access, outcome checks, and allowed context constant before reporting an agent-speed win.

Walk/progress examples failed on the identified older binary. |
| Worth checking / measurement | Search ignore policy, symlinks, binary/Unicode handling, literal versus regex work, sequential/parallel result agreement; compile phase/profile/cache identity; IO cancellation and backend equivalence; iterator early drop, unknown totals, hidden-output overhead; warm/cold initialization; native lifecycle and cross-host layout/accessibility; trace sampling/counting overhead and source coverage. | Existing #2858/#676/#2919, plus bounded findings #2994/#2995/#2997/#3004. No new CLI or syntax is inferred merely because a peer has one. |
| Missing public contract or evidence | Source-range profile detail/method; evidence-backed architecture advice; mapped embedded regions with revision/cancellation; independent-condition evidence; Jet-callable manual progress handles; multi-window close/app lifetime; actual native tray; typed native printing; storage crash/reopen and semantic SQL fuzz evidence. | #2997–#3007 with decisions listed below. #3008 separately owns count semantics, not API availability. |

The claim appendix performs the micro sweep separately for syntax, ergonomics, concrete surfaces, APIs, defaults, errors, tools/commands, UX/DX, expert control, and naming, plus architecture/performance/testing claims. A source with no new item in a category contributes no invented feature. Category summaries are indexes, not substitutes for the individual evidence records.

## Owner ballots and bounded follow-up

All ten ballots are **open, not ratified**. Their full same-workload alternatives, exact proposed APIs, defaults, errors, and reasons live in Tower. Proposed spellings in those cards are not shipped Jet APIs.

| Owner | Decision | Independently decidable choice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #2997 | D-PROFILE-DETAIL1 | Source locations plus function totals, function totals only, or existing evidence only. |
| #2997 | D-PROFILE-METHOD1 | Sampling/counting collection policy, clock and overhead truth, through one recording path. |
| #2998 | D-ARCH-ADVICE1 | Advisory evidence, explicit project policy, or no new architecture-advice product surface. |
| #3003 | D-EMBED-REGION1 | Mapped embedded-region sessions versus whole-document overlays on one frontend. |
| #3002 | D-TEST-MCDC1 | Optional independent-condition evidence versus existing branch/outcome evidence only. |
| #3008 | D-PROGRESS-COUNTS1 | Preserve observed counts, reject inconsistent updates, or retain current completion semantics. |
| #3005 | D-TERM-PROGRESS1 | Public manual progress handles versus iterator-only public progress. Depends on #3008. |
| #2999 | D-UI-WINDOW-LIFE1 | App-owned multi-window lifetime versus the current single-window public boundary. |
| #3006 | D-UI-TRAY1 | Typed tray service with explicit unavailability versus no public tray surface. |
| #3007 | D-UI-PRINT1 | Typed native document-print service versus file export without native print submission. |

The design-away pass removed automatic profiler reruns, a second recording trigger, per-window event loops, host-format parsing in the compiler, a second progress model, and silent capability fallbacks. Sampling is not relabeled as exact counting; a source capture that is partial or unavailable remains so. Print submission is not relabeled as physical completion.

Priority at audit time: first restore trustworthy build and consumer evidence (#2990–#2996); then establish the existing native path (#3004) and hostile storage/testing evidence (#3000/#3001); let the owner decide the independent public-policy choices. These are dated recommendations, not a second work queue. Tower owns the plan, dependencies, criteria, and current status.

## Primary-source checks and unresolved evidence

- [SQLite testing](https://www.sqlite.org/testing.html): fault injection, crash simulation, fuzzing, condition/bit-mask discussion, and the distinction between methods. [LLVM source coverage](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/SourceBasedCodeCoverage.html): condition-independence instrumentation and reporting context.
- [Wails window management](https://v3.wails.io/features/windows/basics/), [application API](https://v3.wails.io/reference/application/), [window source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wailsapp/wails/master/v3/pkg/application/webview_window.go), [tray source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wailsapp/wails/master/v3/pkg/application/systemtray.go), and [releases](https://api.github.com/repos/wailsapp/wails/releases?per_page=10). Old `/features/window`, `/features/printing`, `/features/systray`, and `/llms.txt` routes returned 404; current navigation and implementation source were used instead.
- [tqdm API](https://tqdm.github.io/docs/tqdm/): manual `update`, `close`, `refresh`, `reset`, description/postfix methods, class-level locking/write helpers, and formatting defaults. A docs-only method is not attributed to the video's demo.
- [VS Code embedded-language guidance](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/language-extensions/embedded-languages) and [Volar mapping types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/volarjs/volar.js/master/packages/language-core/lib/types.ts): source mapping, revisions, and service ownership. Jet currently has whole-file overlays; mapped-region cancellation is not inferred from them.
- [Linux perf record](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/perf-record.1.html): collection rate and clock/method control. [The cited architecture skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mattpocock/skills/main/skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md): rule-owning seams and domain vocabulary, not proof that an automated refactor is correct.
- Historical checks include [Dijkstra EWD227](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~EWD/ewd02xx/EWD227.PDF), [Hoare's record-handling source](https://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/text/algol/ACM_Algol_bulletin/1061032/p39-hoare.pdf), [Stroustrup](https://www.stroustrup.com/whatis.pdf), [Nygaard](https://hannemyr.com/cache/knojd_acm78.pdf), [IBM's measurement paper](https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~markhill/restricted/MKreadings2000percaitlin/ibm_jrd_1967_anderson.pdf), and [Stanford's 1971 report](https://bitsavers.trailing-edge.com/pdf/stanford/Stanford_CS_TR_Collection_2025-12-12/PDF/1971/CS-TR-71-204.pdf). Provenance is shared where the talks repeat these sources.
- Unresolved or partial historical access includes the [DTIC alternate](https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/AD0640333.pdf), [Wiley FORTRAN paper](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/spe.4380010203), [ACM archive material](https://archive.org/details/sim_acm-computing-surveys_1974_6_contents/mode/2up), and [Design and Optimization of Compilers](https://archive.org/details/designoptimizati0000vari/mode/2up). Their unavailable contents are not treated as verified facts. OCR of historical slides is explicitly lower-confidence than an accessible original.

The metadata, source identities, timestamp/file locators, claim dispositions, and replay inputs are retained below. Raw captions, comments, downloaded frames, working drafts, and copied board state are temporary captures, not a permanent parallel archive.

### How Rust Made Search 8,000x Faster

The useful mechanism is avoiding work: directory pruning, required-literal filtering, and parallel scanning. The language-branded 8,000x headline does not isolate Rust.

Audience corrections distinguish sorted output, ignore policy, PCRE2 versus default regex, and CPU/SSD saturation. Jet has explicit optional ignore rules and sorted walk results; omitted ignore is not ripgrep’s hidden/Git-ignore default. Preserve that contract. Search parity/measurement stays #2057/#2858; the actual failing consumer is #2994.

### Zig 0.16 IO: Everything You Need to Know

Zig concentrates potentially blocking and nondeterministic operations behind std.Io, with initialization, writer/flush, file, random, sleep, group, testing and backend-selection surfaces.

Audience concerns include boilerplate, allocation, and async-versus-concurrent guarantees. Jet already has direct Core IO, tasks, deadlines/cancellation and testing effects. Do not invent another Io context or VTable. The task-group consumer hit the constructor blocker #2992; scheduler/IO equivalence still needs existing proof owners.

### I Tried to Learn Rust

The learning experience exposes ownership, borrowing, syntax, tooling and repair friction. One learner’s frustration is evidence of a path, not evidence that Rust cannot be learned.

Audience explanations and corrections help locate prerequisites, but popularity is not a usability measure. Jet must teach unfamiliar forms through exact what/why/fix feedback and bounded repairs. Keep its single canonical syntax; measure matched beginner/agent repair tasks through #2481/#2858 rather than copying Rust syntax or asserting a training-corpus advantage.

### Why I Don't Use #!/bin/bash - Shebangs Explained!

Shebangs select a launch program at byte zero; absolute paths, PATH-based env selection, opaque kernel arguments, env -S, and interpreter version are different mechanisms.

The demonstrations and audience portability caveats distinguish Linux, shell, env, and BusyBox behavior. Jet direct executable files already have #1412. No second parser, shell dialect, or automatic env rewrite is recommended. Test installed-path/version behavior through the existing launch contract, not a new shebang feature.

### TypeScript 7.0 is 10x Faster! Why Microsoft Chose Go?!

The TypeScript native-port discussion combines compiler throughput, memory/concurrency, preview delivery, and editor API migration. The 10x claim is a specific project/version claim, not a universal Go-versus-Rust result.

Linked implementation/announcement evidence outranks language-war replies. Jet already owns phase budgets and end-to-end loop measurement. The important uncovered interface is mapped embedded-language clients over one frontend, #3003; compiler-speed checks stay #676/#2858. Preview/version/install/editor spellings remain separate micro records.

### How To De-Slop A Codebase Ruined By AI (with one skill)

A concrete ordering rule is spread across optimistic and persisted paths. Deepening the insertion-point seam is useful only if it owns that rule and reduces required agreement.

The audience challenges one-more-skill framing, source-text tests, file-count metrics and premature architecture. Jet’s score-zero disagreement is the counterexample; #2998 owns optional advice, #2991 the broken lint fixture, and #2992 the failed clock seam. Strategic, operational and tactical answers are given separately above.

### Casey Muratori – The Root of The Root of All Evil – BSC 2026

The historical argument concerns program frequency, workload evidence and how optimization advice acquired a simplified folklore. Measurement scope, count versus sample, clocks and source attribution matter more than the slogan.

Linked papers and historical slides have varying accessibility and OCR quality. Retain the gap rather than completing a quotation from memory. Jet should extend its existing trace path with bounded source-hotspot evidence, #2997, with separate detail and collection-method choices. No unqualified universal cost percentage or automatic rerun is proposed.

### Casey Muratori – The Big OOPs: Anatomy of a Thirty-five-year Mistake – BSC 2025

The talk separates boundaries, abstraction and historical object ideas from the later habit of making class hierarchy the default design tool. Simula/record handling and quoted historical material are distinct sources.

The audience disputes historical framing and supplies alternative interpretations. The two Casey talks count as one speaker identity where relevant. Jet should keep ordinary data, functions, traits and modules available without adding inheritance dogma or banning a useful domain hierarchy. Rule ownership connects to #2998; storage/Pool correctness is not proved by architecture rhetoric.

### Wails V3: Go’s Best GUI Framework (Electron Killer?)

Wails V3 separates application setup from windows and services, improves multi-window and development integration, and exposes platform operations around a webview application.

Current docs/source corroborate architecture, not every performance or packaging claim. Wails has real operations Jet currently lacks. #2999/#3004/#3006/#3007 own the native gaps; existing #2962/#2465/#2478/#2792 own typed endpoints, preserved state and platform services. The direct comparison above avoids a duplicate renderer or web framework.

### Reliability Lessons From SQLite - Richard Hipp | SSW 2026

SQLite combines regression tests, fault injection, crash/reopen simulation, fuzzing, differential/semantic oracles and coverage. These methods expose different failure classes and can invalidate one another’s false confidence.

Audience corrections and official testing docs keep MC/DC, bit masks and machine-object coverage distinct. Jet already has fault effects and branch rows; do not duplicate them. Add storage crash/reopen cases (#3000), semantic SQL fuzz cases (#3001), and let the owner decide optional independent-condition evidence (#3002).

### Web dev is finally healing

The web argument favors tighter feedback between reactive state and asynchronous work, including pending state and ordering; HTML-driven interactions offer a different boundary from component-local state.

The creator caption track is the exception to the automatic-caption corpus. Solid and HTMX release/source checks separate demonstrated APIs from version opinion. Jet already has pending boundaries, HMR and typed endpoint derivation. Prove stale-result, cancellation, error and preserved-state transitions under #2478/#2465/#2962; do not introduce a second reactive mechanism.

### I Write Python Like THIS and now Everyone Hates Me

The Python demonstration compresses layout and expressions through semicolons, implicit joining, comprehensions, lambdas, globals and recursive/generator forms. Character count does not measure comprehensibility or equivalent evaluation order.

Audience criticism is useful when it names side effects, order, debugging or lost names; style preference alone does not establish a defect. Jet should retain its direct named-function/control-flow spelling and formatter rather than add golfing alternatives. Existing diagnostic/tooling and matched repair-loop measurement own the transferable lesson.

### Why C++ Static Variables Secretly Use Mutexes

C++ dynamic block-static initialization has a one-time guard protocol; constant initialization, dynamic initialization and steady-state checks are not the same cost.

Primary language/ABI/runtime sources and the fresh compiled contrast correct the mutex shorthand and AI-assembly risk. Jet’s compile-time static values and development persistence are not C++ lazy-local initialization. No new lazy-static syntax or unsafe guard opt-out is proposed; initialization performance belongs in measured existing cells.

### "tqdm" is Awesome in Python

tqdm makes progress cheap to adopt through iterator wrapping, inferred or explicit totals, descriptions, formatting and terminal adaptation; its full API also supports manual lifecycle and multiple bars.

Docs-only methods are not attributed to the video. Jet already has iterator progress and a richer host model. #3005 ballots a public manual API; #3008 independently ballots count truth. #2995 owns the rejected current example. Dynamic descriptions, typed columns, output separation, cleanup, cancellation and update cost remain individual claims, not one “progress exists” verdict.

## Validation and closeout evidence

- All 1,019 claim records parse as JSON, use the declared enums, have unique record/topic identities, cover all ten micro categories for every source, and have either an existing Tower owner or an explicit no-action reason. No actionable record is assigned to a done card.
- Tower publication was read back byte-for-byte. Its 19 JSON evidence blocks retain the coverage, visual locators, six replay inputs, thirteen proof-receipt groups, fourteen source ledgers, and exact-topic matrix.
- `scripts/agent/jet-env node scripts/agent/check-audit-dispositions.mjs` read **1,039 dispositions in this report with no errors attributed to it**. The repository-wide command exited 1 because it also found 68 errors in older reports: missing disposition tables and missing historical card/decision records. This is not a repository-wide green claim.
- `scripts/agent/jet-env node plugins/tower/tower.mjs lint --docs` also exited 1 on existing idle claims, stale drafts, duplicate suspects, and missing specification references. It reported no error against the nineteen new cards or ten new ballots. Those unrelated records were not rewritten or falsely closed.
- The source checker now reports all fourteen video IDs as `tracked` in the prior-art registry. Its exit 3 is the deliberate already-mined rejection; no rerun approval or second capture was performed.
- All nineteen new cards were read back in `planning`; all ten ballots were read back `open` with no outcome. Only the report-delivery card #2989 is eligible for closure. Compiler/library implementation, ratification, native-platform completion, and peer performance victory are not claimed by this audit.

## Retained evidence appendix

The following JSON blocks retain the normalized ledgers and compact proof receipts. Paths under the former capture root are provenance locators, not promises that scratch files remain. Replay inputs are included; substitute a new disk-backed scratch path when rerunning them. Source/video links remain independently usable.

Claims are dated observations, not a live feature inventory or a replacement for Tower. `owner` identifies the canonical work home; `action: none` plus `disposition_reason` records evidence with no remaining action. No appendix entry ratifies a ballot. The matrix groups equal propositions, not merely similar words. Shared Casey Muratori provenance is counted once. The five cross-resource repeats are analytic comparisons, not five independent benchmark replications. Source/audience disagreements resolved by primary evidence remain explicit in each claim’s correction and in the report above; no unresolved exact-topic conflict remains after review.

    "action": "The owner selects the source-profile contract through its complete ballot; no ratified trace or privacy rule is reopened. A hot/cold program yields correctly attributed source evidence; changing its source invalidates attribution.
